y-m-60-03.title: How many digits of approximation fit we trust?
y-m-60-03.topic: Approximate common logarithm and number of digits: how far fit we trust approximation?
y-m-60-03.goal: Learn say small error in approximation fit change conclusion as n get bigger, find cases wey conclusion differ, and state when approximation fit be trusted.
y-m-60-03.material: We want find how many digits dey inside 2ⁿ. Number of digits for positive integer N na (integer part of log N) + 1, so number of digits of 2ⁿ na (integer part of n × log 2) + 1. Actual value of log 2 na 0.30102999566…, but Soyoung use approximation 0.301 and find number of digits by adding 1 to integer part of n × 0.301. (Integer part na the whole number before decimal point. Example: integer part of 9.03 na 9.)

y-m-60-03.s.s1.prompt: For n=30, Soyoung talk say 30 × 0.301 = 9.03, so 2³⁰ get 10 digits. We fit trust this conclusion? Multiply 30 by actual value 0.30102999566…, compare, then choose.

y-m-60-03.s.s1.o.a: Since we use approximation, error dey, so we no fit know number of digits until we calculate with exact value
y-m-60-03.s.s1.r.a: Actual value don already show, so when you compare both products you go know size of error. Think whether error big enough to change the conclusion.
y-m-60-03.s.s1.o.b: 9.03 farther from integer 9 than the error (less than 0.001), so the conclusion say 10 digits stand
y-m-60-03.s.s1.o.c: The approximation smaller than actual value, so actual number of digits always go one more than the number found with approximation
y-m-60-03.s.s1.r.c: A value wey small small no mean say integer part must change. Think wetin must happen before integer part fit change.
y-m-60-03.s.s1.o.d: 0.301 and actual value agree to third decimal place, so number of digits go same for any n
y-m-60-03.s.s1.r.d: When you multiply, the error go grow n times. Compare n=30 with one very big n.
y-m-60-03.s.s1.explain: 30 × 0.30102999566… = 9.0309… and 30 × 0.301 = 9.03, so the difference less than 0.001. Both values dey between 9 and 10, so integer part na 9 for both, and 2³⁰ get 10 digits (2³⁰ = 1073741824). Whether approximation fit trusted depend on size of error and how far the calculated value dey from an integer.
y-m-60-03.s.s2.prompt: Find and enter two different natural numbers n wey number of digits of 2ⁿ from Soyoung method (using 0.301) and from actual value (using 0.30102999566…) no be the same. (Number of digits = integer part of n × log 2 + 1)

y-m-60-03.s.s2.hint.1: Calculate some values to see how difference between n×0.301 and n×(actual value) dey change as n increase.
y-m-60-03.s.s2.fail.c1: n must be natural number wey at least 1.
y-m-60-03.s.s2.ok.c2: The number of digits from both methods different.
y-m-60-03.s.s2.fail.c2: The number of digits from both methods na the same. Compare integer parts of n×0.301 and n×0.30102999566.
y-m-60-03.s.s2.explain: When n=196, 196 × 0.301 = 58.996 get integer part 58, so e say 59 digits; but with actual value, 196 × 0.30102999566… = 59.0018…, so integer part na 59 and 2¹⁹⁶ get 60 digits. Same thing happen for n=299 (91 digits) and n=392 (119 digits). When calculated value dey just below an integer, small error fit make am cross the integer or no cross, and the conclusion go change.
y-m-60-03.s.s3.prompt: For n=30, we fit trust approximation, but no be for n wey you just find. For one or two sentences, write wetin separate cases where number of digits from approximation 0.301 fit be trusted from cases wey e no fit.

y-m-60-03.s.s3.hint.1: Compare that distance with n×(actual value−0.301).
y-m-60-03.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You say error grows as n grows?
y-m-60-03.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You say risk high if calculated result sits just below/above integer?

y-m-60-03.s.s3.model.0: Approximation error is multiplied by n, so larger n gives larger error. When n×0.301 is very near integer, error may move it across or not, changing digit count. Far from integer, result is safer.
y-m-60-03.s.s3.model.1: For n=30, 9.03 far from integer, so about 0.001 error won't change integer part. For n=196, 58.996 near 59, a small difference changes digit count.
y-m-60-03.s.s3.modelNote.1: It doesn't state error grows with n, but captures key point by comparing distance to integer with error.

y-m-60-02.goal: Learn say 'every example I check work' no be enough proof for general claim, make counterexample by yourself, and identify the conditions wey you need before you conclude.

y-m-60-01.material: Suho solve equation log₂(x²) = 4 (x na nonzero real number) as dem show below. (How to read: log₂ A mean 'logarithm of A with base 2', and x² mean 'x squared'.)

Line 2 leave out case x<0, so the claim for line 5 say 'only one' na wrong conclusion. You fit also accept line 5 as the wrong line. Even x = −4 give log₂ 16 = 4.

y-m-60-01.s.s2.fail.c2: The value of log₂(x²) no be 4. Think again about which power of 2 go give x².
y-m-60-01.s.s2.explain: By the definition of logarithm, x² = 2⁴ = 16, so x = 4 or x = −4. Both values satisfy the original equation, so two solutions dey.
y-m-60-01.s.s3.prompt: One change like Suho line 2 fit change the allowed range of x. Choose every change below wey keep 'the range of values x fit take' the same before and after. (x na real number.)

y-m-60-07.material: Sequence {aₙ} has partial sum Sₙ=n²+2n+3 (n natural). Eunwoo solution below. (aₙ means nth term; Sₙ sum through n; Sₙ₋₁ sum through n−1.)
